title: Legal Powers Analyzer
description: Document-by-document extraction and analysis pipeline that identifies attorneys-in-fact, powers, amount limits and validity in legal powers of attorney.
problem: Reviewing a power-of-attorney deed means reading the whole document to find who can sign, up to what amount and until when. The assistant extracts those four facts and generates a downloadable Word summary for the legal team.

architecture.caption: Four-layer pipeline: input, application and storage, AI processing, and a cross-cutting security and observability layer.

nodes.name: Legal team
nodes.detail: Uploads the deed and defines the query

flow: The legal team opens the Streamlit app hosted on App Service and selects the case or branch to work on.
The document is stored in Blob Storage, which also holds configuration and prompt templates.
Document Intelligence processes the file and returns text, tables and structure, even on scanned deeds.
Azure OpenAI applies the use-case prompt: identifies attorneys-in-fact, powers, amount limits and validity.
The result goes back to the app for review and download as a Word report, with the original kept in Blob Storage as backup.

components.name: Document Intelligence
components.role: Text and structure extraction from the legal document.

components.name: Azure OpenAI
components.role: Classification, summary and extraction of powers.

components.name: Azure Key Vault
components.role: Custody of AI service and Storage keys.

insight.title: No search index, on purpose
insight.text: It uses neither Azure AI Search nor Cosmos DB: each document is processed in isolation against Document Intelligence and Azure OpenAI. It is a deliberate difference from the conversational assistants, and the reason for a noticeably smaller service footprint.
